Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports and pull requests as a burden:

**Daniel Stenberg (curl)**
Daniel Stenberg, the founder of curl, has been one of the most vocal maintainers regarding the burden of AI-generated reports. He described the influx of invalid AI-assisted vulnerability reports as equivalent to a DDoS attack, noted that they have never received a valid AI-generated bug report, and ultimately shut down curl's bug bounty program due to the mental toll.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai_bug_reports/267311 | QUOTE: "We now ban every reporter instantly who submits reports we deem AI slop. A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: AI-generated bug reports are overwhelming the curl project and wasting maintainers' time.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against_time_wasting_ai_bug_reports/267311 | QUOTE: "He went on to say that the project has never received a single valid bug report that was generated using AI, and their rate is increasing." | CLAIM: No AI-generated bug reports submitted to curl have been valid.
SOURCE: https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/ai-agents-spam-the-volunteers-securing-open-source-software | QUOTE: "The never-ending slop submissions take a serious mental toll to manage and sometimes also a long time to debunk. Time and energy that is completely wasted while also hampering our will to live." | CLAIM: Managing AI-generated bug reports causes significant mental toll and burnout for maintainers.
SOURCE: https://mastodon.social/@bagder/113618036640872539 | QUOTE: "You submitted what seems to be an obvious AI slop…" | CLAIM: Stenberg directly confronted submitters about AI slop on Mastodon.

**Seth Larson (Python)**
Seth Larson raised concerns about AI "slop" reports in the Python ecosystem, emphasizing that even though they are bogus, they require time from trained eyes to investigate, leading to maintainer burnout.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action_against_time_wasting_ai_bug_reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports." | CLAIM: AI-generated security reports cause stress, confusion, and isolation among maintainers.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action_against_time_wasting_ai_bug_reports/267311 | QUOTE: "In many ways, these low-quality reports should be treated as if they are malicious. Even if this is not their intent, the outcome is maintainers that are burnt out and more averse to legitimate security work." | CLAIM: Low-quality AI reports effectively act as malicious contributions that burn out maintainers.

**Mitchell Hashimoto (Ghostty)**
Mitchell Hashimoto of the Ghostty project expressed extreme frustration with the AI slop affecting his project, eventually implementing a zero-tolerance approach for AI-generated contributions from non-maintainers.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "It’s a fucking war zone out here man. Maintainer morale at an all time low. I totally empathize with the projects that flip the table and ban all AI. I’m getting close to saying only maintainers and accepted issues can have any AI ." | CLAIM: The influx of AI contributions is severely damaging maintainer morale.

**Steve Ruiz (tldraw)**
Steve Ruiz closed all external pull requests for tldraw after the project was overwhelmed by AI-generated contributions. He noted that submitters would put apparent effort into PRs but never return to sign the CLA, and discovered that his own AI-generated issue scripts were being fed into other users' AI tools to create "AI slop all the way down."

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "We would get PRs from people who seemed like they put a lot of work into this PR, but they would never reply to sign the contributor license agreement, and it was like, 'Man, you put all this time into this code, and then, you just never came back to the thread, like, what?' That’s very unusual," | CLAIM: AI-generated PRs often lack the follow-through of genuine human contributions.
SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "My low-effort issues were becoming low-effort pull requests, with AI doing both sides of the work." | CLAIM: AI tools can generate slop on both the issue creation and PR sides, compounding the problem.

**Marty Haught (RubyGems)**
Marty Haught noted a tenfold increase in the volume of reports, many looking valid at first glance, which has made reviewing them highly burdensome.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "It takes time, if you get 20 or 50 of these in a week, that could be a full day just reviewing that, where it was maybe 15 minutes previously, and so, now, what do we do?" | CLAIM: The volume of AI-generated reports drastically increases the time required for maintainers to review submissions.

**Dax (Twitter handle @thdxr)**
A user posting on Twitter under the handle @thdxr reported receiving a spam of AI-generated security advisories that distracted from real reports.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "someone opened up 7 security advisories today all of which did not make sense in the context of our project all clearly AI generated this gets in the way of use responding to actually valid reports that are made by people who understand our project" | CLAIM: AI-generated security reports obstruct maintainers' ability to respond to actual, valid reports.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Direct URLs to Mitchell Hashimoto's or Seth Larson's original posts (the sources cite their statements, but the specific URLs to the original blogs/posts/tweets were not included in the search results).
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The specific identity/project affiliation of the Twitter user @thdxr beyond their quote.
